# S-2 · Control Tailoring

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | S Select (system level) |
| Phases | PH-TMRR (primary) |
| Depends on | S-1 |
| Inputs | ART-BASELINE, ART-RA, ART-BIA, EXT-CNSSI1253-OVERLAYS, ART-INV, ART-ORG-CONTEXT, ART-REQ, EXT-ORG-POLICY |
| Outputs | ART-BASELINE (updates) |
| Writes facts | — |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-PM, PER-CCP, PER-ISSM · A: PER-PM · C: PER-AO, PER-IO, PER-ISSE, PER-PRIV, PER-ISSO · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-CCP](../../personas/PER-CCP.md), [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-AO](../../personas/PER-AO.md), [PER-IO](../../personas/PER-IO.md), [PER-ISSE](../../personas/PER-ISSE.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-ISSO](../../personas/PER-ISSO.md) |

Purpose: Tailor the selected controls into the tailored control baseline by applying overlays, designating common controls, scoping, compensating, assigning DoD parameter values and supplementing.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** S-1 is done: `baseline.json` exists and `facts.yaml#baseline_id` has
   `set_by_task: S-1`. Why: tailoring starts from the selected baseline (CNSSI 1253
   §3.2.2), never from a list the agent builds.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`, then the tailoring procedure:
   `uv run rmf refs show CNSSI1253 --section "3.2.2"` (the seven required activities) and
   `uv run rmf refs show SP800-53B --section "2.4"` (the tailoring activities). Note which
   overlays the categorization lists (the facts block of ART-CAT) and which risks in ART-RA
   point at controls.
3. **Interview** PER-ISSM, then PER-CCP (`## Interviews`). Cover each tailoring activity:
   - **overlays:** which apply and why, and any conflict between two overlays (the AO and
     the privacy officer resolve those, CNSSI 1253 §3.2.2 item 2);
   - **privacy controls** (a system processing PII): interview PER-PRIV with PER-ISSM on
     each tailoring action that touches a privacy control, and record in ART-BASELINE
     `## Privacy tailoring` that the tailoring leaves no gap in compliance with privacy
     requirements and adds no privacy risk;
   - **common controls:** which baseline controls the provider covers (S-3 records the
     allocation; S-2 only notes that the control stays in the baseline);
   - **scoping:** baseline controls that do not apply to this system's technology,
     environment or mission, with the reason;
   - **compensating controls:** a baseline control the system cannot implement, and the
     control that gives equivalent protection;
   - **parameter values:** the organization-defined values (ODPs) of the baseline controls,
     from organizational policy (ART-ORG-CONTEXT) first, then the ISSM;
   - **supplementation:** controls or enhancements to add for risks in ART-RA or
     requirements the baseline does not cover (S-1 lists them in ART-BASELINE).
   - **assumptions:** each assumption in `framework/baselines/tailoring-inputs.yaml`
     (the SP 800-53B §2.3 and CNSSI 1253 §2.4 assumptions, plus those of each applied
     overlay): does it hold for this system? A baseline assumption that fails
     (`when: holds-false`) sends you back to scoping, compensating, supplementing or an
     overlay; an assumption the baselines do not address that holds (`when: holds-true`,
     such as classified information or a cross-domain link) is revisited: name the
     controls that address it, whether already in the baseline or supplemented, or the
     overlay, or record `outcome: revisited-no-change` with the rationale when the selected
     controls already address it. A Space Platform Overlay assumption (AS-SPC-1 to
     AS-SPC-10) that fails revisits the Associated Controls the overlay tailors out on it:
     add them back with a tailoring action, or record `outcome: revisited-no-change` with the
     rationale for keeping them out (TLR-003);
   - **assurance:** whether additional assurance-related controls are needed to reach the
     trustworthiness the system requires (CNSSI 1253 §3.2.2 item 3.f.5). Read which
     controls contribute with `uv run rmf catalog show --control <id> --fields title,assurance`;
   - **overlay conditions:** for an applied overlay that lists `overlay_conditions` in the
     same file (the Classified System Overlay's wireless, mobile devices, external systems
     outside the U.S. and data tainting), whether each condition applies;
   - **law and policy:** for every control you would remove or compensate for, the laws,
     regulations and policies (OMB policy among them) that carry it. A control they require
     stays in; a control is never tailored out because it is hard to implement. For a
     control an applied overlay specifies, read its Section 6 specification first:
     `uv run rmf catalog show --run <run> --control <id> --fields title,overlay` prints the
     justification, guidance, parameter values and the authorities its references cite.
     The laws, regulations and policies among them (`authorities`) can require the control,
     so a removal tests each of them and names it in `law_policy.authorities` (OVS-001); the
     guidance documents (`guidance references`, NIST SPs and the like) require nothing;
   - **controls an overlay says not to select:** the Privacy Overlays justify not selecting
     AC-2(8) (dynamic account management) for every control set. Such a control is selected
     only after coordinating with the SAOP or designee (PER-PRIV): record
     `privacy_coordination` (`by: PER-PRIV`, or a designee's persona with `designee_of: PER-PRIV`;
     the `finding`; `sources`) on the `add` or
     `specification` action that keeps it (OVS-002);
   - **controls with a Privacy Implementation Considerations checkmark:** each selected control
     `framework/baselines/privacy-considerations.yaml` marks (CNSSI 1253 Appendix D, and Table 1
     of the Classified System Overlay when applied) may introduce privacy risk. Before it is
     implemented, the system owner confers with the SAOP or designee (interview PER-PRIV):
     record `privacy_implementation` (`control_id`, `by: PER-PRIV` or a designee with
     `designee_of: PER-PRIV`, the `implications` of its checkmark addressed, the `finding` with
     any additional steps to protect privacy, `sources`), one record per control (PIC-001);
   - **specification:** controls whose statement lacks the detail needed to implement them,
     and the organization-defined specification information to add.
4. **Write `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml`** whole (schema
   `framework/schema/tailoring.schema.json`). One record per action:

   ```yaml
   actions:
     - control_id: ac-2
       action: parameter
       parameter:
         param_id: ac-02_odp.10
         value: "quarterly"
       rationale: "Account reviews follow the ISSO's quarterly review cycle."
       sources: [INT-014.A2]
     - control_id: sc-7.4
       action: add
       rationale: "Supplements the baseline for the external interface risk in ART-RA."
       sources: [INT-014.A4, ART-RA]
   ```

   - `action` is `add` (supplement), `remove` (scoped out), `compensating` (with
     `compensating_for: <control>`), `parameter` (with `parameter.param_id` and `value`) or
     `specification` (with `specification.text` and `placement: statement|addendum`).
   - Record `assumptions` (one entry per applicable assumption: `id`, `holds`, the
     `controls` whose actions answer a failed assumption or that address an applying one,
     the `overlays` applied for it, or `outcome: revisited-no-change` for an applying one or a
     failed Space Platform Overlay assumption whose tailored-out controls stay out), `assurance` (`additional_needed`, with an `add` action marked
     `assurance: true` on a catalog assurance control when it is true) and, for an overlay
     with conditions, `overlay_conditions` (`overlay`, `condition`, `applies`). TLR-003 to
     TLR-005 check them.
   - A `remove` action names its `basis` (`scoping`, `no-risk` or
     `circumstance-not-applicable`) and, for scoping, `scoping.consideration`. A
     `security-objective` downgrade adds `downgrade` (the one or two `objectives` the control
     supports, `sources` including ART-RA, `security_relevant_unaffected: true`); the
     CNSSI 1253 column of each objective at its own level must not select the control.
   - Every `remove` and `compensating` action carries `law_policy` (`reviewed`: all of
     legislation, regulation, policy and omb-policy; `requires_control`; the `authorities`
     read). A control a requirement requires for this system is neither removed nor
     compensated (TLR-002). With basis `circumstance-not-applicable` the requirement applies
     only in circumstances this system lacks, so `authorities` must name it, and
     `requires_control` is not read.
   - A `compensating` action names the baseline control it stands in for (the SSP must not
     record that control as `implemented`), `source: catalog` (the default) or `other`
     (with `other_control` and a `catalog_search` that found `no-suitable-control`),
     `cannot_implement`, `equivalence`, and `risk` (assessment resting on ART-RA, accepted
     by the AO or its designated representative: PER-AO or PER-AODR, since only the
     authorization decision itself is non-delegable). A catalog compensating control joins the baseline (origin `compensating`),
     so S-4 writes its SSP statement (TLR-001).
   - Get parameter IDs from `uv run rmf catalog show --control <id> --fields params`; never
     invent one. An applied overlay's parameter values (`--run <run> --fields params,overlay`)
     are assigned here or in the S-4 statement; they align with, and never replace, the
     other values CNSSI 1253 indicates. OVS-003 checks only that a value is recorded for
     each ODP the overlay assigns; whether it is the overlay's value is the ISSM's call.
   - Remove a control only on a risk-based determination, never because it is hard to
     implement (CNSSI 1253 §3.2.2 item 4). A control the system cannot implement and gets
     no compensating control stays in the baseline: S-4 records it as `planned`, and its
     risk reaches the POA&M (item 7).
   - If the file was seeded, read it first and keep its records, adding yours.
   Why: `rmf baseline resolve` applies the `add` and `remove` actions, so this file is the
   one home of the tailored baseline.
5. **Re-resolve the baseline.** `uv run rmf baseline resolve <run>` regenerates
   `baseline.json` with the add/remove actions applied (origin `tailored-in` for added
   controls). Its `baseline_id` must still equal `facts.yaml#baseline_id`: the ID names the
   selection basis (method, categorization and the configured `control_subset` size), never
   the post-tailoring count, so tailoring cannot change it. If they differ anyway, stop and
   journal a NOTE, because something other than tailoring changed the selection basis, and
   that fact belongs to S-1. Why: each fact has exactly one writer (INV-4).
6. **Update `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`.** Append `S-2` to `touched_by` and rewrite the
   `## Tailoring and allocation` section's tailoring part: the overlays applied, the counts
   per action, and every `remove` and `compensating` action by control ID with its reason,
   traced to the same tokens as the records. Do not copy all the parameter records; name
   the file. Keep every other section as S-1 wrote it.
   Note the C-SCRM decisions taken here (which supply chain controls are selected, tailored
   or removed, their cost and the cost of not implementing them, FedRAMP first for a cloud
   service provider, and the controls of each procurement chosen with information security
   personnel): S-4 records them in `artifacts/data/scrm-plan.yaml` `controls` (SCRM-010).
   Only PER-AO accepts the risk of removing a control.
7. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-2`,
   until 0 errors. `rmf build` writes the OSCAL profile from the new `baseline.json`.
8. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-ISSM | responsible (R) | overlays, scoping decisions, parameter values, supplementation for ART-RA risks |
| PER-CCP | responsible (R) | which baseline controls the provider's common controls cover, and their parameter values |
| PER-PRIV (when PII is processed) | consulted (C) | the Privacy Overlay's applicability, which the privacy official approves (CNSSI 1253 §3.2.2 item 1) |
| PER-PM (optional) | accountable (A) | acceptance of the tailoring decisions and the cost of supplemented controls |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects PER-ISSM and PER-CCP interviews.

## Inputs

- `baseline.json` (selected controls; generated, read only)
- `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`
- `artifacts/ART-CAT.md` (categorization and overlays in the facts block)
- `artifacts/ART-RA.md` (risks that justify supplementation or scoping)
- `artifacts/ART-ORG-CONTEXT.md` (organizational parameter values, tailored baselines),
  when the run has it
- `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml`, when seeded
- Control text and parameters: `uv run rmf catalog show --control <id> --fields statement,params`
- Overlays (EXT-CNSSI1253-OVERLAYS): `uv run rmf refs show CNSSI1253 --section "2.5"`, then
  the overlay's own reference, for example `uv run rmf refs show CNSSI1253F-ATT6-PRIVACY --section "1"`

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml` | — | schema `tailoring`, written whole |
| `baseline.json` | — | regenerated by `rmf baseline resolve`; never edited |
| `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md` | `touched_by: [S-1, S-2]` | updated (updater) |

## Facts

S-2 writes no facts. `baseline_id` belongs to S-1 (step 5).

## Done when

- `tailoring.yaml` holds every tailoring action with a rationale and sources, and every
  parameter value the interviews set.
- `baseline.json` is current (GEN-STALE-001) and still matches `facts.yaml#baseline_id`.
- ART-BASELINE lists S-2 in `touched_by` and summarizes the tailoring.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-2` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task S-2`, with the action counts (add, remove,
  compensating, parameter) and the overlays applied.
- DECISION: an overlay conflict resolved by the AO or privacy official,
  `## <time> · DECISION · task S-2 · by: <PER-ID> (simulated, INT-###.A#)`.
- The baseline-ID stop in step 5 is a NOTE, not a workaround.
